definition: Diligent means showing steady, careful effort in one's work.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word diligent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know diligent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The most diligent volunteer showed up every Saturday for two years, rain or shine.
Dutiful is weaker — a dutiful worker does what is required and no more; a diligent one brings steady, careful effort that goes beyond mere obligation.
Tireless is stronger than diligent: it suggests effort that never flags at all, day or night, while diligence is sustained but human-paced.

Industrious means hardworking by habit - an industrious person is always busy, always producing, filling the hours with output. Diligent adds care to the effort: the work is not only steady but attentive, done properly with nothing skipped. An industrious worker impresses by how much gets done; a diligent one by how carefully.

Hardworking means putting in consistent effort - long hours, real exertion, no slacking. Diligent describes the quality of that effort as much as the quantity: steady work carried out carefully, again and again, over time. A hardworking student puts in the hours; a diligent one also checks every answer before handing the test in.

Diligent means showing steady, careful effort in one's work.
Nobody noticed Priya's routine at first.
She arrived at the community garden twenty minutes early each week, watered on a strict rotation, and logged what she planted in a small notebook.
When aphids appeared, she researched remedies that evening and applied them the next morning.
Season after season she kept it up without being asked or reminded.
Three years later, hers was the only plot that had never once failed — the quiet reward of diligent work.
Priya's steady, careful effort maintained week after week for years — early arrivals, strict rotations, prompt problem-solving — is exactly what makes her diligent.
neutral, admiring; report-card and workplace staple
Diligent praises steady, ongoing effort across time — showing up and doing careful work again and again.
Its close cousin in this unit, painstaking, praises something narrower: the intense care poured into the fine details of one particular task.

The historical society hired two interns for the summer to digitize its photograph collection, several thousand images in all, before the originals faded any further.
Jonah scanned at speed, and by the middle of July his file count was nearly double Priya's.

Priya worked differently, and the archivist called her diligent: she cleaned each negative before scanning, entered the date and donor for every file, and re-checked the day's uploads each evening before logging off.
In August the director sampled both sets and found dozens of Jonah's files mislabeled or blurred, while Priya's held a single error in more than a thousand images.
Both interns were thanked at the end of the season, but it was Priya's routine the society printed in its handbook for future volunteers.
